# Validation record

Date: 2026-10-10. Scope: the unified `pawse/` app and its new voice, agent and evidence interfaces. This is not a certification of the imported backend.

## Passed

- 57 automated tests with synthetic HTTP responses. Coverage includes warning signs, provider failure/deadlines, consent, image/audio validation, bounded streaming, session ownership, shared care/run cache, safe phone links, clinic normalization/ranking, legacy authorization, the seven-role workflow, exact policy citations, Gradium clone/localize/preview/save/delete contracts and synthetic scenario arithmetic.
- JavaScript syntax checks for both `app.js` and `voice.js`, formatting, HTML identifier binding checks and generated OpenAPI export.
- Real API access checks: `gemini-3-flash-preview` text, synthetic PNG and silent WAV; `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` text; `gemini-embedding-001` embeddings. Each returned HTTP 200 with the expected response kind. See [sanitized results](model-access-check.json).
- Browser walkthrough at the existing narrow in-app viewport: all six Mimi clinic-path scenes; slot review and explicit demo approval gates; CHF 385 clinic / CHF 510 home estimates; taxi script and claim checklist.
- Browser multilingual integration: a fictional Chinese message produced a German script with English subtitles through live Gemini. The translated script preserved the instruction to ask the price without making a booking, and included the AI-assistant disclosure.
- Browser agent integration: a no-consent run visibly skipped external providers; an opt-in synthetic routine-checkup request returned real Gemini guidance and a completed care-agent trace in approximately 4.7 seconds, with clinic search skipped because location consent was off.
- Missing Gradium configuration visibly disables paid voice operations while retaining the recording setup interface. Frontend review fixed replacement-recording races and overlap with voice operations.

Browser timings are isolated observations, not latency guarantees. Model smoke checks establish access, not clinical accuracy or multilingual speech quality. One Starlette/httpx test-client deprecation warning remains; the tests pass.

## Not verified or not connected

- Gradium live cloning, German localization, TTS and speaker similarity: no Gradium key was supplied. Provider contracts are mocked; no owner sample has been uploaded.
- Microphone permissions, real microphone capture and local uploaded-audio playback still require a manual browser check. An automated file-chooser attempt timed out, so no successful browser audio-upload test is claimed.
- Chinese, English, German and Hindi recognition quality with representative human recordings. The API audio smoke check used silence only.
- Live clinic discovery: no Mapify backend URL or Google Places key was supplied. Only provider adapters and normalization are tested.
- Telephone transport, audio injection into a mobile call, actual calendar checks, appointment/taxi booking and claim submission are not connected. Mimi's calls and policy decisions are explicitly synthetic.
- Real owner-policy ingestion and vector RAG: the current retrieval baseline is lexical and searches only the reviewed fictional corpus. Legacy book collections and OpenAI/Chroma indexes remain excluded.
- Imported device/report services, live video ingestion, desktop-width visual QA and public multi-user deployment have not been validated in this iteration.

`gemini-2.5-flash` appeared in the model listing but returned HTTP 404 for generation in this project. Credentials and recordings are not included in test fixtures or publication artifacts.

## Goal
Build the browser side of the Gemini Live voice session: the owner talks to the cat, hears Pawse answer in real time, sees the transcript and what tools are running. The backend is done and verified against the real API (#18, PR #21).

## Contract
Everything you need is in [`docs/GEMINI_LIVE.md`](https://github.com/yyyuanfish/pawse/blob/feat/gemini-live/docs/GEMINI_LIVE.md): the two endpoints, the message flow and the audio formats. Short version:
1. `POST /api/v1/live/tokens` `{share_with_gemini: true, language}` gives `{token, model}`.
2. `@google/genai` from a pinned CDN ES module: `new GoogleGenAI({apiKey: token, httpOptions: {apiVersion: "v1alpha"}})`, then `ai.live.connect(...)`.
3. On each `toolCall`, POST each function call to `/api/v1/live/tool-calls`, send `response` back with `sendToolResponse`, and render `ui`.

- [ ] Playback: gapless 24 kHz PCM16 queue; flush on `interrupted` so the owner can talk over Pawse.
- [ ] Live transcript (input and output transcription) and a status chip per tool call.
- [ ] Render tool `ui`: clinics and care summary, policy evidence, German script with subtitles.
- [ ] `confirm_call`: confirm dialog, then open the `tel:` link only if the owner confirms.
- [ ] Failure messages (token, socket closed, mic denied) with a fallback to the recorded/typed flow.

## Done when
In Chrome: say "My cat Mimi is limping after jumping from a wardrobe, which vets are nearby?", hear a spoken answer, see the transcript and the `assess_and_find_vets` chip, and talk over Pawse to interrupt it.

Proposed stack: Gradium streaming STT → `gemini-3-flash-preview` (text + tools) → Gradium streaming TTS, rather than Gemini Live.

Reasons:
- Gradium does µ-law 8 kHz in/out natively, so no transcoding is needed for Twilio (#4).
- We can speak in the owner's cloned German voice from `voice.py`; Gemini Live can't use a cloned voice.
- Tool calling stays in text Gemini.
- Barge-in via Gradium's semantic VAD.

Next: latency/German-accuracy spike, results posted here.
Spike results (real Gradium API, `scripts/gradium_spike.py` on `feat/voice-calling`). Each sentence was synthesized over the TTS WebSocket, then streamed back into the STT WebSocket at real-time pace, in phone audio (ulaw 8 kHz) both ways.

| # | Lang | TTS first audio | TTS total | Audio | STT end of turn (after speech) | STT last text | WER |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | de | 239 ms | 4658 ms | 8.6 s | 15 ms | 261 ms | 4% |
| 2 | de | 237 ms | 2256 ms | 6.2 s | 85 ms | 228 ms | 22% |
| 3 | en | 205 ms | 2979 ms | 5.4 s | 63 ms | 401 ms | 0% |

Notes:
- Speech starts about 0.2 s after the text is sent, so callers hear Pawse almost immediately.
- Gradium's VAD flags the end of a turn within 0.1 s, and the final words arrive within 0.4 s.
- Most of #2's 22% WER is formatting: "sechzehn Uhr dreissig" came back as "16.30 Uhr". The first word ("Wir") was also dropped.
- #1's only error is the brand name: "Pawse" → "Pause".
- The input was clean synthetic speech. Real phone audio and real speakers still need testing in the live call (#4).

Estimated reply delay on a call: about 0.4 s of STT, plus Gemini's first sentence, plus 0.2 s of TTS. Gemini latency gets measured next.

Decision: go with Gradium STT → `gemini-3-flash-preview` → Gradium TTS for live calls.

# Demo video recorder

Records the 2-minute demo as a 1920x1080 video, scripted and repeatable, so a re-take after a UI change takes a
single command and no screen-recording session. Same pipeline as our SwissHacks 2026 DRIFTWATCH recorder.

The page being recorded is currently a **mock** ([`mock/index.html`](mock/index.html)): a static page that plays the
"Mimi is limping" story from [the demo script](../research/pet-insurance/demo-video-script.md) with canned lines,
cards and timings. It has no backend, model, calls or bookings. It shows a "DEMO MOCK · SIMULATED CALLS" pill, so
it is never mistaken for working features.

## Run

Node 20+, Python 3 (serves the mock), and ffmpeg on `PATH` for the mp4 (optional; without it you still get the webm).

```sh
cd demo
npm install
npx playwright install chromium   # first time only
npm run record:demo
```

Output in `demo/demo-out/` (git-ignored):

| File | What |
| --- | --- |
| `pawse-demo.mp4` | The deliverable: opening load trimmed, h264, synthesized click/glide soundtrack |
| `pawse-demo.webm` | Raw Playwright take, keeps the browser load |
| `trim.json`, `events.json` | Cut point and action log the post-step uses |

Knobs (environment variables):

- `SPEED=1.5`: faster take. It scales both the spec's holds and the mock's own pauses. The default (1) runs about 85 s.
- `DEMO_LOOPS=2`: repeat the clean pass, for a looping clip on a slide.

To preview the mock by hand: `npm run mock`, then open http://127.0.0.1:4173.

## How it works

1. [`e2e/demo-recording.spec.ts`](e2e/demo-recording.spec.ts) drives the page like a user would: it taps the mic, picks
   reply chips and chooses option A, with a visible cursor that glides along curved paths. Each `expect()` doubles
   as a smoke test, so a missing story beat fails the take. The spec writes where the load ends (`trim.json`) and
   every click and glide (`events.json`).
2. [`scripts/finalize-demo.mjs`](scripts/finalize-demo.mjs) trims the head, renders a soundtrack from the
   action log ([`scripts/demo-audio.mjs`](scripts/demo-audio.mjs), deterministic, unit-tested by `npm test`), and muxes
   it onto the mp4.

The voiceover and the simulated German call audio are not part of this pipeline. Add them in the video editor on top
of the mp4.

## Swapping the mock for the real app

Once the real app can run the story end to end, point `baseURL` and `webServer` in
[`playwright.config.ts`](playwright.config.ts) at it (for example `uvicorn pawse.app:app --port 8765`). Then keep the
same element names (`Talk to Pawse` button, reply chips, `#opt-a`, `data-state`) or update the locators in the spec.

# Pawse Controller–Frontend Contract

This document maps the current screens to backend controllers. It defines what the frontend sends, what it may display as confirmed, and how it handles incomplete work. For payload details, follow the domain contracts below.

## 1. Global conventions

- **Base URL:** `/api/v1`, on the same origin as the app. Send JSON for POST bodies; read the response content type before treating it as JSON, SSE or WAV.
- **Session:** retain the `pawse_session` cookie across requests. It isolates local results and voice IDs; it is not an account or authentication system. API tools must use a cookie jar to reproduce a browser workflow.
- **Configuration:** only server-side code receives API keys. `/health` reports local process health; `/capabilities`, `/agents/graph` and `/voice/status` report configuration and supported flows, not successful live provider checks.
- **Consent:** care AI, location sharing, Gemini voice processing, Gradium sharing and own-voice consent are separate choices. Do not infer one from another.
- **Validation:** unknown request fields are rejected. The mutation body limit is 4,500,000 bytes; decoded photos and WAV inputs are each limited to 3,000,000 bytes.
- **Persistence:** keep recordings, photos and care data out of browser analytics and persistent browser storage. Responses use `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The implementation is the static app in [pawse/static](../pawse/static/) with controllers in [pawse/app.py](../pawse/app.py), [orchestration.py](../pawse/orchestration.py), [voice.py](../pawse/voice.py) and [knowledge.py](../pawse/knowledge.py).

## 2. Screen-to-controller map

| Screen/action | Method and path | Success | Frontend responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Startup/configuration | `GET /health`, `GET /capabilities` | 200 JSON | Distinguish configured, unavailable and verified behavior |
| Care form, streamed mode | `POST /care/requests?stream=true` | 200 SSE | Display safety immediately; merge events until the final result |
| Care form, single response | `POST /care/requests` | 201 `CareResult` | Display useful results even when status is `partial` |
| Agent mode | `GET /agents/graph`, `POST /agents/runs` | 200 graph; 201 run | Render roles and the final execution trace |
| Retrieve/delete summary | `GET` / `DELETE /care/requests/{request_id}` | 200 / 204 | Use the same session; remove deleted results from the UI |
| Dictation and call draft | `POST /voice/transcriptions`, `POST /voice/scripts` | 200 JSON | Let the owner review transcript, facts and subtitles |
| My voice | Voice clone/localization routes | JSON or WAV | Follow the [voice state sequence](controller-voice-contract.md) |
| Generate German audio | `POST /voice/speech` | 200 WAV | Play/download after user action; do not label as a completed call |
| Demo policy evidence | `POST /knowledge/search` | 200 `KnowledgeResult` | Show synthetic scope, exact snippets and citations |
| Mimi rehearsal | `GET /demo/mimi` | 200 JSON | Keep simulated replies, costs and arrangements visibly labeled |
| Existing CatAgent chat/report | `POST /agent/requests` | 200 SSE | Render wrapped legacy events and stream-level failures |

Full paths add the `/api/v1` prefix. Singular `/agent/requests` is the legacy bridge; plural `/agents/runs` is the new coordinator.

## 3. Care form, results and clinic cards

Submit either a direct `CareRequest` or an `AgentRunRequest` containing `{ "care": CareRequest }`. Do not submit both for one interaction: they share the active-work limit and would duplicate provider calls. The current interface supports selecting the workflow.

The [care contract](controller-care-contract.md) defines valid input and events. Store the returned `request_id`; an agent run's care ID is `response.care.request_id`. A follow-up answer currently requires a new request containing the updated concern. There is no conversation-turn or case-update endpoint for care navigation.

Render `assessment.urgency` independently from provider progress. An urgent warning must remain visible during loading and failure. Follow-up questions are questions for the owner/vet, not a confirmed diagnosis. The API's language pattern is broader than the current UI's `en`, `zh`, `de`, `hi` options; built-in fallback and some explanatory text remain English.

| Result field | Rendering rule |
| --- | --- |
| `status: partial` | Show available guidance, contacts and warnings; offer an explicit retry |
| `clinics: []` | Show no retrieved matches; do not invent nearby practices |
| `open_now: null` | “Opening hours unconfirmed”; never convert null to open or closed |
| `distance_km` | Label as straight-line distance, not driving time or ETA |
| `call_url: null` | No dial action; display the supplied phone as text if present |
| `services` / `services_to_ask_about` | Keep reported clinic data separate from suggested questions |
| `insurance.coverage` | Always display `unconfirmed` for the current live care route |
| `handoff` | Editable/reviewable facts for a later script request, not a message already sent |
| `search_url` / `maps_url` | Open only on user action |

Clinic cards are populated from the care result. There is no Pawse clinic-detail, reviews, map-tile or booking endpoint. Any future map uses the returned coordinates and retains the same source/unknown-state labels.

## 4. Progress and agent trace

Use `fetch` to consume POST SSE; native `EventSource` issues a GET and cannot submit this body. Decode incrementally, retain incomplete chunks, split complete frames at the blank line, and parse the `data:` JSON. See the exact [event table](controller-care-contract.md#3-streaming-contract).

Use `type` as the discriminator. Provider events may finish in either order. A `created` event does not mean the result is already retrievable. A connection closed before `result` is incomplete; there is no stream replay, event ID or guaranteed background completion. Do not automatically resubmit after a dropped stream because POST has no idempotency key.

`/agents/runs` returns a final JSON snapshot, not incremental trace events. Show a pending run state while awaiting it; do not animate fabricated agent completions. Trace `elapsed_ms` is an offset from run start, not the duration of an individual model call. Run completion does not unlock unconnected call, appointment or calendar actions. See the [agent contract](controller-agent-contract.md).

## 5. Voice, evidence and rehearsal handoffs

1. Record/transcribe input, then let the owner correct it before passing it to care or script generation. An empty transcript means no usable speech was recognized.
2. Review the care handoff and choose `vet`, `insurer` or `taxi` before requesting a German script. Retain paired subtitles and `draft_not_sent` status.
3. Use the own-voice recording and localization flow in the [voice contract](controller-voice-contract.md). A standard voice is an explicit selection, not an automatic replacement.
4. Read speech responses as blobs. Revoke replaced object URLs and stop microphone tracks after recording, cancellation or page exit.
5. Display policy snippets using the [knowledge contract](controller-knowledge-contract.md). The current demo corpus must not change a live owner's insurance status.
6. Keep the Mimi story's recorded steps separate from live responses. A scene's fictional 16:30 appointment is not a calendar event or confirmed reservation.

## 6. Errors and retention

The frontend must accept the existing error shapes:

| Shape | When |
| --- | --- |
| `{ "error": { "code": "validation_error", "fields": [...] } }` | 422 field validation; each field has `location` and `message` |
| `{ "detail": "..." }` | Controller/provider HTTP exceptions such as 409, 429, 502 or 503 |
| `{ "error": "cross_origin_request_rejected" }` | Middleware rejects a mutation's Origin, HTTP 403 |
| `{ "error": "request_too_large" }` | Middleware body bound, HTTP 413 |
| SSE `{ "type": "error", "code": "legacy_agent_unavailable", "message": "..." }` | Legacy failure after a stream has opened |

Treat 404 on summary retrieval as absent, expired or inaccessible. A 409 voice response means a prerequisite is missing or the action is out of sequence. A 429 means wait for the active operation; keep current input available. Care-provider errors generally arrive inside a successful HTTP response with a `partial` result.

Completed summaries share a maximum of 100 in-memory entries and a 15-minute lifetime, with expiry pruned on subsequent requests. Restart clears them. Voice IDs have a separate lifecycle: clearing a summary does not delete provider voices. See [voice retention](controller-voice-contract.md#6-deletion-and-retention).

## 7. Frontend handoff checks

- Exercise complete, partial, empty-list, no-consent, expired-result and provider-error views.
- Confirm real SSE progress and final-only agent traces are presented accurately.
- Complete record → clone → localize → preview → save → speech with mocks; record real provider verification separately.
- Check keyboard controls and narrow layouts while preserving the existing pink/gray palette in `style.css`.
- Keep transcripts and provider/model output as text; never insert them as trusted HTML.

# Gemini Live voice session

Pawse holds a real-time voice conversation with the owner through the Gemini Live API (`gemini-3.8-live`). While it talks, Gemini calls Pawse tools, and those tools run the existing backend features. The browser holds only a short-lived, single-use token. The permanent `GEMINI_API_KEY` stays on the server.

```
Browser                     Pawse backend                         Gemini Live
  | POST /live/tokens ------->| mint token locked to model,          |
  |<-------- {token, model} --|   prompt and tools (v1alpha) ------->|
  | ai.live.connect(token) --------------------------------------->|
  | mic PCM 16 kHz ----------------------------------------------->|
  |<--------------------------------- audio 24 kHz + transcripts ---|
  |<---------------------------------------------- toolCall --------|
  | POST /live/tool-calls --->| runs care / policy / script tool     |
  |<-- {response, ui} --------|                                      |
  | sendToolResponse(response) ----------------------------------->|
  | render ui (clinics, script, confirm dialog)                      |
```

## Backend (implemented)

### `POST /api/v1/live/tokens` → 201

Request: `{ "share_with_gemini": true, "language": "en" }`. `language` is `en`, `zh`, `de` or `hi` and sets the language Pawse starts in. Consent is required (422 without it).

Response:
```json
{ "token": "auth_tokens/...", "model": "gemini-3.8-live", "api_version": "v1alpha",
  "expires_at": "...Z", "new_session_expires_at": "...Z",
  "tools": ["assess_and_find_vets", "search_policy", "draft_vet_call_script", "open_clinic_call"] }
```

- The token works for one session (`uses: 1`). The session must start within 60 seconds, and the token expires after 30 minutes.
- The server locks the model, system prompt, AUDIO output, input and output transcription, and the tool declarations into the token. The browser can't change them.
- Errors: 503 when there is no key, 502 when Gemini refuses (safe message only), 429 after 10 sessions per 10 minutes per browser session. The rate limit is per Google project and shared by the team.

### `POST /api/v1/live/tool-calls` → 200

Request: forward each `functionCall` from the `toolCall` message as is, plus browser context:
```json
{ "id": "<functionCall.id>", "name": "<functionCall.name>", "args": { ... },
  "share_with_gemini": true,
  "context": { "language": "en", "cat_name": "Mimi", "share_location": true, "location": { "lat": 47.37, "lng": 8.54 } } }
```
Send `location` only when the owner has turned on location sharing.

Response: `{ "id", "name", "response": { ... }, "ui": { ... } | null }`.
- **`response`** goes back to Gemini unchanged: `session.sendToolResponse({ functionResponses: [{ id, name, response }] })`. Tool failures come back as `response.error` with HTTP 200, so the conversation can continue.
- **`ui`** is the full data to show:

| Tool | What it runs | `ui` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `assess_and_find_vets` | The agent workflow (`/agents/runs`): care guidance plus ranked clinics | `{ care: CareResult, trace: AgentTrace[] }` |
| `search_policy` | `/knowledge/search` (demo corpus, cited) | `KnowledgeResult` |
| `draft_vet_call_script` | The reviewed German script logic behind `/voice/scripts`, with subtitles in `context.language` | `CallScript` |
| `open_clinic_call` | Looks up a clinic from this session's last search | `{ action: "confirm_call", clinic_name, phone, call_url }` |

**`confirm_call` is an app gate:** show a confirm dialog, and only open `call_url` (`tel:`) if the owner confirms. Pawse never places or joins the call.

Errors: 422 for an unknown tool or missing consent. 429 when 3 tool calls are already running for this session (15 globally).

`GET /api/v1/voice/status` also reports `live_configured` and `live_model`.

## Frontend: to do (Nami, #6)

1. Load `@google/genai` as an ES module from a pinned CDN version (`cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@google/genai@<exact version>/+esm`), and connect with `new GoogleGenAI({ apiKey: token, httpOptions: { apiVersion: "v1alpha" } })` and `ai.live.connect({ model, config: { responseModalities: ["AUDIO"] }, callbacks })`.
2. Mic: `getUserMedia` with an AudioWorklet that downsamples to **16 kHz mono PCM16**, then `session.sendRealtimeInput({ audio: { data: base64, mimeType: "audio/pcm;rate=16000" } })`.
3. Playback: model audio is base64 **24 kHz mono PCM16** in `serverContent.modelTurn.parts[].inlineData`. Queue it gaplessly on an `AudioContext`. When `serverContent.interrupted` arrives, flush the queue so the owner can talk over Pawse.
4. Process every part of every message: `inputTranscription` and `outputTranscription` fill the transcript panel, and `toolCall` shows a status chip per tool. Tools are non-blocking, so Pawse keeps talking while they run.
5. Explicit Gemini consent before starting. Clear messages when minting fails, the socket closes or the mic is denied, with a fallback to the existing recording and typed flow. End the session cleanly before the token expires (a demo is 2 minutes, so there's no resumption).

## Verified (2026-10-10)

Against the event key with `gemini-3.8-live`: a token was minted through REST, a session opened on the constrained v1alpha endpoint, and a text turn ("My cat Mimi is limping after jumping off a wardrobe") made Gemini call `assess_and_find_vets`. `/live/tool-calls` ran the workflow, the result was sent back, and Gemini answered in audio with transcripts, using the tool result. Browser microphone capture and playback are not built yet (see above).

# Git push (`/gp`)

## Pre-flight

1. `gh auth status` (fails: `gh auth login`, GitHub.com, HTTPS, browser).
2. `git status --porcelain`. Anything uncommitted: run [commit-secure](../commit-secure/SKILL.md) first.
3. `bash scripts/check.sh` must be green. It is the gate: CI is on request and `main` has no branch
   protection, so nothing else stops a red build reaching teammates.

## Which mode

- **Push to main:** a small change inside your own module (see the module table in
  [docs/AGENT_DEVELOPMENT.md](../../../docs/AGENT_DEVELOPMENT.md)), or the user says "push directly".
- **PR:** you touch shared integration files (`pawse/app.py`, request/response models,
  `docs/openapi.json`, `schemas/pawse.ts`, requirements, README), or the user asks for a PR.

## Push to main

1. `git fetch origin && git pull --rebase origin main`. Conflicts: resolve, re-run the check,
   `git rebase --continue`. Unsure whose change wins: ask, do not guess.
2. `git push origin HEAD:main`.
3. Report the commit URL: `gh browse -n "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"` prints it.

## PR + squash-merge

1. **Existing PR?** `gh pr view --json number,url,state 2>/dev/null`. One open for this branch: push to it.
2. **On main?** Branch first: `git checkout -b <feat|fix|chore|docs>/<short-name>`.
3. **Sync:** `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main`, then `bash scripts/check.sh`.
4. **Push + open:** `git push -u origin HEAD`, then `gh pr create --base main --title "<type: what>" --body-file <tmpfile>`
   using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (what changed, how verified, known gaps).
5. **CI only on request:** if the user asks for CI, `gh workflow run check --ref <branch>`, then `gh run watch`.
   Red: `gh run view <id> --log-failed`; fix, push, re-run.
6. **Merge:** after a green local check (and green CI, if it was requested), `gh pr merge <n> --squash --delete-branch`, then confirm
   `gh pr view <n> --json state` says `MERGED`.
7. Report the full PR URL (`https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>`), not just `#<n>`.

## Safety

- Never `git push --force` to `main`; on your own branch only `--force-with-lease`.
- Never merge with a red local check or a red requested CI run.

## Keep this skill current

Update when branch rules, CI checks or the merge method change. Run `python scripts/validate_skills.py` after editing.

"""Synthetic audio for the browser tests: no human voice, no recordings in git.

`speechlike` is a harmonic tone with a syllable-rate envelope, loud enough that a silent or broken
capture path is obvious. Real-speech checks use human recordings from PAWSE_RECORDINGS_DIR instead.
"""
import base64
import io
import math
import struct
import wave


def speechlike(seconds=6.0, rate=48000, channels=1, peak=0.4):
    frames = bytearray()
    for i in range(int(seconds * rate)):
        t = i / rate
        envelope = 0.5 + 0.5 * math.sin(2 * math.pi * 4 * t)  # ~4 syllables per second
        tone = sum(math.sin(2 * math.pi * f * t) / n for n, f in enumerate((180, 360, 540, 720), 1))
        sample = struct.pack("<h", int(32767 * peak * envelope * tone / 2.1))
        frames += sample * channels
    return to_wav(bytes(frames), rate, channels)


def silence(seconds=1.0, rate=16000):
    return to_wav(b"\0\0" * int(seconds * rate), rate, 1)


def to_wav(frames, rate, channels):
    out = io.BytesIO()
    with wave.open(out, "wb") as f:
        f.setnchannels(channels)
        f.setsampwidth(2)
        f.setframerate(rate)
        f.writeframes(frames)
    return out.getvalue()


def read_wav(data_b64):
    """Decode a base64 WAV from a request body: (channels, sample width, rate, seconds, rms 0..1)."""
    with wave.open(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(data_b64))) as f:
        channels, width, rate, n = f.getnchannels(), f.getsampwidth(), f.getframerate(), f.getnframes()
        raw = f.readframes(n)
    samples = struct.unpack(f"<{len(raw) // 2}h", raw) if width == 2 else ()
    rms = math.sqrt(sum(s * s for s in samples) / len(samples)) / 32768 if samples else 0.0
    return channels, width, rate, n / rate, rms


def pcm16_rms(data_b64):
    raw = base64.b64decode(data_b64)
    samples = struct.unpack(f"<{len(raw) // 2}h", raw[: len(raw) // 2 * 2])
    return math.sqrt(sum(s * s for s in samples) / len(samples)) / 32768 if samples else 0.0

# Browser and real-speech tests (issue #25)

These tests replace the manual browser checklist in [docs/VALIDATION.md](../../docs/VALIDATION.md): microphone
capture, audio upload, desktop layout, the Gemini Live client, and recognition of real English, Chinese, German and
Hindi recordings. They were written **before** the new frontend (#6, Gemini Live client #22), so the Playwright tests
are red until the UI exposes the hooks below. Build the UI to turn them green.

## Run

```bash
pip install -r requirements-e2e.txt && python -m playwright install chromium
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e                    # browser tests, no keys, providers mocked
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e --headed -k live   # watch one group
```

`bash scripts/check.sh` skips the browser tests (no `PAWSE_E2E`) and runs only the always-on speech-metric tests.
Layout screenshots land in `test-results/layout/` (git-ignored) for a human look.

How the tests work without hardware or keys:

- **Microphone:** Chromium's fake capture device plays a synthetic, speech-like WAV as the mic, so a silent or
  broken capture path fails (the old smoke test used silence only).
- **Gemini Live:** the Live WebSocket (`wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/...`) is answered by a fake server in
  the test, using the real `@google/genai` wire format. `/live/tokens` and `/live/tool-calls` are mocked.
- **Server:** the real app runs with all provider keys blanked. `/voice/transcriptions` is mocked per page, and every
  captured upload is also checked with the server's own WAV validator (`pawse.voice.inspect_wav`).
- Every browser test also fails on any console error.

## Frontend contract

Hooks are `data-testid` attributes, listed in [frontend_contract.py](frontend_contract.py). Rename one there, here
and in the UI in the same commit.

| `data-testid` | Element and behaviour the tests expect |
| --- | --- |
| `language` | `<select>` with `en`, `zh`, `de`, `hi`; sent as `language` with transcriptions and Live tokens |
| `consent-gemini` | Checkbox. Without it, nothing is sent to `/voice/transcriptions` or `/live/tokens` and the status names Gemini |
| `record` | Toggle button, `aria-pressed="true"` while recording. Mic tracks end after stop |
| `audio-upload` | `<input type="file" accept="audio/*">` |
| `audio-preview` | `<audio>` with a `src` once a usable recording exists; no `src` after a rejected file |
| `transcribe` | Sends the current recording as mono 16-bit WAV |
| `voice-status` | `role="status"`/`"alert"`. Errors say what to do next (permission denied: mentions microphone and upload; bad file: mentions "seconds" or "audio"; Live token failure: mentions recording) |
| `message-input` | Editable `<textarea>`. The transcript lands here; typing always works, also after failures |
| `talk` / `end-talk` | Start and end a Gemini Live session |
| `cat` | `data-state`: `idle` → `listening` (connected) → `speaking` (model audio) → back to `listening` on `interrupted`; `error` on token failure or dropped socket; `idle` after End |
| `transcript` | Panel with `transcript-owner` and `transcript-pawse` entries, rendered as text, never HTML |
| `tool-chip` | One per tool call, `data-tool="<name>"`, `data-status`: `running`, `done`, `error` |
| `confirm-call` | `role="dialog"` for `open_clinic_call`, showing the clinic name |
| `confirm-call-accept` | An `<a href="tel:…">` with the tool's `call_url`; no `tel:` link exists outside the open dialog |
| `confirm-call-cancel` | Closes the dialog |
| `results` | Care guidance, clinics, policy evidence, scripts. At 1280 px and wider it sits beside `transcript`; on a phone it stacks below |
| `demo` | Starts the Mimi rehearsal |
| `simulated-label` | On every simulated step, visible once the rehearsal starts |

Layout rules, at 1280, 1440, 1920 and 390 px: no horizontal scroll; no overlapping controls; controls at least
24×24 px (inline text links exempt); on desktop, `talk` and `record` are above the fold and content spans at least
60% of the width.

Audio rules: recordings 0.5 to 60 s, any sample rate or channel count in, mono 16-bit WAV out; nothing audio-like in
`localStorage`/`sessionStorage`, no IndexedDB. Live: ephemeral token in the socket URL (never `key=`), mic as
`audio/pcm;rate=16000` at real-time pace, tool calls forwarded with `share_with_gemini` and `context.language`, no
`context.location` without location consent, `toolResponse` echoes the call `id`, `name` and `response`.

## Real recordings (opt-in, spends Gemini quota)

```bash
PAWSE_LIVE_SPEECH=1 PAWSE_RECORDINGS_DIR=/mnt/pawse-recordings python -m pytest tests/e2e -k real   # API path
PAWSE_E2E=1 PAWSE_LIVE_SPEECH=1 PAWSE_RECORDINGS_DIR=/mnt/pawse-recordings python -m pytest tests/e2e -k real_speech
```

Needs `GEMINI_API_KEY` in the environment or `.env`. Recordings are personal data: collect them with the speaker's
consent, keep them off git (for example on `/mnt`), and delete them when the check is done.

`manifest.json` in that directory:

```json
{ "recordings": [
  { "file": "de-01.wav", "language": "de", "reference": "Meine Katze Mimi hinkt seit dem Sprung vom Schrank.",
    "speaker": "s1", "device": "laptop mic" }
] }
```

- At least 3 recordings per language (`en`, `zh`, `de`, `hi`), ideally different speakers and devices.
- Mono 16-bit PCM WAV, 0.5 to 60 s, up to 3 MB: `ffmpeg -i in.m4a -ac 1 -ar 16000 -sample_fmt s16 de-01.wav`.
- `reference` is exactly what was said. Write numbers the way they are spoken, since scoring is literal.

Pass bar ([speech_metrics.py](speech_metrics.py)): word error rate at most 0.15 (en), 0.20 (de), 0.30 (hi), and
character error rate at most 0.20 (zh). Chinese must come back in Han characters and Hindi in Devanagari, not
romanized or translated. Silence must give an empty transcript. Per-recording results are written to
`test-results/speech-api.json`; copy the summary into `docs/VALIDATION.md`.

# React frontend and backend agent integration

Checked on 10 October 2026. The React app lives in `web/`. Build with `npm ci --prefix web && npm run build --prefix web`, then start FastAPI. Open `/app/?live=1` for backend tools or `/app/?demo=1` for the simulated rehearsal. Vite development uses the configured `/api` proxy. Credentials remain server-side.

| Frontend role | Actual endpoint | Result and boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REST fallback voice input | `POST /api/v1/voice/transcriptions` | Browser recordings converted to mono WAV; Gemini transcription. Microphone starts only after the owner enables it. |
| Care / vision / orchestration | `POST /api/v1/agents/runs` | `{care: CareRequest}`; consumes nested `care`, `trace`, `actions`. Text and selected photos require Gemini consent. Video stays local. |
| Vet discovery | `POST /api/v1/care/requests` | Generic veterinary query, location consent, no symptoms and no AI consent. Preserve backend ranking, unknown hours, source and retrieval time. |
| Communication | `POST /api/v1/voice/scripts` | Owner-reviewed facts, separate consent, German draft with EN/ZH/DE/HI subtitles. No recipient replies or bookings. |
| Policy evidence | `POST /api/v1/knowledge/search` | Explicit demo-policy panel; English lexical search and original citations. No private-policy ingestion or coverage approval. |
| Speech | `POST /api/v1/voice/speech` | Reviewed draft, separate Gradium consent, selected approved own voice or explicitly selected standard voice. Binary WAV with playback/download; no silent fallback. |
| Native Live conversation | `POST /api/v1/live/tokens`, Gemini WebSocket, `POST /api/v1/live/tool-calls` | Native PCM audio and transcripts; locked ephemeral token; backend tool results. |
| Voice enrollment | React home → Record my voice | Local 10–25 second recording, clone/localization/preview/save and approved German emergency rehearsal. |

The new live handoff uses `LiveHandoff.jsx` and `agents/handoff.js`. It bypasses the older story-backed `livePhoneAgent.js`; the explicit “Open simulated Mimi phone rehearsal” button opens that helper with Gradium sharing initially off. The owner can then enable the teammate’s whole-call Gradium rehearsal. All recipient replies/results remain simulated. Mock phone agents remain rehearsal-only. A validated `tel:` link opens the owner's dialer; audio is not injected into calls.

The language selector offers EN/ZH/DE/HI. German and Hindi use English UI labels where translations are not supplied; their API language and subtitle codes are preserved. Live conversation now uses the Gemini WebSocket client and native audio. `?live=1&voice=rest` explicitly selects the older transcription/browser-speech fallback. No automatic voice substitution occurs.

## Evaluation

- `PYTHON=.venv/bin/python bash scripts/check.sh`: safety, skill catalog, JavaScript, all `web/scripts/check-*.mjs`, OpenAPI consistency, backend pytest.
- `npm run check --prefix web`: mock story contracts, clinic mapping, voice workflow, legacy rehearsal helper, real handoff consent/languages/errors, service-worker private-response exclusion.
- `npm run build --prefix web`: production compilation.
- A bounded actual-HTTP smoke check against a local server without credentials verified seven-role workflow traces, local policy citations, explicit missing clinic configuration, missing Gemini and unconfigured own-voice errors. No paid provider calls occurred.
- Browser walkthrough verified the React consent gate, typed care request, agent result entry and separate insurer preparation page. See `VALIDATION.md` for the final observed browser result.

There is no independent evaluation agent in this repository. Open PR #29 contains proposed browser/audio tests for older test hooks; it has not been merged or claimed green here. Real microphone capture, speech accuracy (EN/ZH/DE/HI), human multilingual Live conversation, Gradium clone quality and actual telephony are separate evaluations. They cannot be established by mocked contract checks or a successful build.

## Data boundary

The OSM crawling snapshot remains an offline staging dataset under the crawling contract. It is not relabelled as a live provider or silently shown as verified clinics. With no Places key or external clinic backend, the React page displays a configuration/unavailability error. Integrating OSM requires an explicit provider/schema change and reviewed cat-clinic evidence.

The service worker caches only the app shell/assets, not API responses, query URLs or no-store responses. Old Pawse shell caches are cleared on activation.

## Native voice and own-voice testing

See [the manual test guide](VOICE_TESTING.md). Native transport tests cover PCM/resampling, transcripts, all audio parts, interruptions, tool round trips, consent, mute/end and failure handling. Own-voice operations use the existing backend contracts; no schema changed.

"""Recorded audio in the React app: the REST voice fallback and the own-voice enrollment recorder.

The fake microphone loops 2.5 s of speech-like sound and 2.5 s of silence, so voice-activity detection
sees a turn start and end. Uploaded WAVs are also checked with the server's own validator.
"""
import pytest
from playwright.sync_api import Page, expect

from audio_fixtures import read_wav
from e2e_helpers import DENY_MIC, MIC_RELEASED, TRACK_SPY, wait_for
from pawse.voice import inspect_wav

REST = "/app/?live=1&voice=rest"


def start_rest_call(page: Page):
    page.route("**/api/v1/agents/runs", lambda r: r.fulfill(status=503, json={"detail": "Gemini is not configured."}))
    page.goto(REST)
    page.locator(".start-btn").click()
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Agree and start").click()
    page.locator("nav.call-controls button").first.click()  # microphone on


def test_rest_fallback_sends_one_audible_mono_wav_per_spoken_turn(page: Page, transcriptions):
    start_rest_call(page)
    wait_for(page, lambda: transcriptions, seconds=25, what="a transcription request after a spoken turn")
    body = transcriptions[0]
    assert body["language"] == "en" and body["share_with_gemini"] is True
    channels, width, rate, seconds, rms = read_wav(body["audio"]["data"])
    assert (channels, width, rate) == (1, 2, 16000)
    assert 2 <= seconds <= 8, f"turn of {seconds:.1f}s: expected the 2.5 s utterance plus the silence that ended it"
    assert rms > 0.02, "the uploaded turn is silent: the capture path lost the microphone signal"
    inspect_wav(body["audio"]["data"])
    expect(page.locator(".cap-user")).to_contain_text("Mimi is limping")


def test_rest_fallback_sends_the_chosen_language(page: Page, transcriptions):
    page.goto("/app/?live=1&voice=rest")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="中文").click()
    start_rest_call(page)
    wait_for(page, lambda: transcriptions, seconds=25, what="a transcription request")
    assert transcriptions[0]["language"] == "zh"


def test_rest_fallback_with_denied_microphone_is_explained(page: Page, transcriptions):
    page.add_init_script(DENY_MIC)
    start_rest_call(page)
    expect(page.locator(".cap-error")).to_contain_text("Couldn't open the microphone")
    expect(page.get_by_role("textbox")).to_be_enabled()
    assert transcriptions == []


def open_own_voice(page: Page):
    page.goto("/app/")
    page.get_by_role("button", name="Record my voice · emergency rehearsal").click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("heading", name="My voice · emergency rehearsal")).to_be_visible()


@pytest.mark.parametrize("seconds", [11])
def test_own_voice_recording_plays_back_locally_and_sends_nothing(page: Page, seconds):
    page.add_init_script(TRACK_SPY)
    uploads = []
    page.on("request", lambda r: r.method == "POST" and "/api/v1/voice/" in r.url and uploads.append(r.url))

    expect(page.locator("audio[controls]")).to_have_count(0)

    page.get_by_role("button", name="Record my voice", exact=True).click()
    expect(page.get_by_role("alert")).to_contain_text("Microphone unavailable")
    expect(page.get_by_role("button", name="Record my voice", exact=True)).to_be_enabled()

import os
import time
import wave

import pytest

from e2e_helpers import fake_mic_args, serve
from speech_metrics import LANGUAGES, TARGETS, error_rate, in_native_script, live_speech_enabled, load_manifest

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(bool(live_speech_enabled()), reason=live_speech_enabled() or "")
FIRST = {e["language"]: e for e in reversed(load_manifest())}  # first recording of each language
CHIP = {"en": "EN", "zh": "中文", "de": "DE", "hi": "हिन्दी"}


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def live_app():
    proc, url = serve(dict(os.environ))  # keeps GEMINI_API_KEY
    yield url
    proc.terminate()
    proc.wait(10)


def settled_caption(page, seconds):
    """The owner caption once it has stopped changing for 3 s (Gemini streams it in pieces)."""
    end, last, since = time.monotonic() + seconds, "", time.monotonic()
    while time.monotonic() < end:
        text = page.locator(".cap-user").first.text_content() if page.locator(".cap-user").count() else ""
        if text != last:
            last, since = text, time.monotonic()
        elif text and time.monotonic() - since > 3:
            return text
        page.wait_for_timeout(250)
    return last


@pytest.mark.parametrize("language", LANGUAGES)
def test_spoken_message_survives_the_live_call(browser_type, live_app, language):
    entry = FIRST.get(language)

    with wave.open(str(entry["path"])) as f:
        seconds = f.getnframes() / f.getframerate()
    browser = browser_type.launch(args=fake_mic_args(entry["path"], loop=False))
    try:
        page = browser.new_page(base_url=live_app, permissions=["microphone"], viewport={"width": 1440, "height": 900})
        page.goto("/app/?live=1")
        page.get_by_role("button", name=CHIP[language], exact=True).click()

# Browser and real-speech tests (issue #25)

Automated versions of the manual checks in [docs/VALIDATION.md](../../docs/VALIDATION.md): microphone capture,
audio upload, desktop layout, the Gemini Live voice client, and recognition of English, Chinese, German and Hindi
speech. They drive the shipped pages: the React app at `/app` (built from `web/`) and the original page at `/`.

## Run

```bash
pip install -r requirements-e2e.txt && python -m playwright install chromium
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e                      # ~90 browser tests, no keys, ~2 min
PAWSE_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e -k live_voice --headed   # watch one file
```

The first run builds `web/dist` if it is missing (needs Node). After changing `web/`, run `npm run build --prefix web`
so the tests see your change. `bash scripts/check.sh` skips the browser tests and runs only the speech-metric tests.
Layout screenshots land in `test-results/layout/` (git-ignored) for a human look.

## What runs, and how without hardware or keys

| File | Page | What it proves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `test_browser_live_voice.py` | `/app/?live=1` | Consent before any token; ephemeral token on the constrained socket; mic off until the owner turns it on; audible 16 kHz PCM at real-time pace; mute sends `audioStreamEnd` and stops audio; transcripts as text (no HTML); model audio plays and an interruption flushes it; typed text goes over the socket; tool calls forwarded once, answered and rendered; `open_clinic_call` only offers the dialer; token failure, denied mic and dropped socket are explained; hang-up and drops release the mic |
| `test_browser_recording.py` | `/app/?live=1&voice=rest`, own voice | REST fallback: one audible mono 16 kHz WAV per spoken turn, accepted by the server's validator, in the chosen language; own-voice recorder plays back locally, uploads nothing, rejects under 10 s; denied mic explained |
| `test_browser_upload.py` | `/` | Audio upload (the React app has none): 48 kHz stereo, 44.1 kHz and 8 kHz WAVs play locally and are sent as mono 16-bit; too short, too long and non-audio files are explained and never sent; a new upload replaces the old; a recorded message is audible |
